structured_output.hypothesis: If all domestic pigeon breeds descend from Columba livia and its geographic sub-species, then genome-wide variation across breeds sampled from the fancy pigeon lineages will form one intraspecific cluster with no breed deeply diverged from the rest, and no breed will fall outside the C. livia reference's diversity range.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using SNPs called from the whole-genome resequencing runs linked to BioProject PRJNA167554, across all breed samples with at least 5x coverage: (a) the maximum pairwise autosomal nucleotide divergence between any two breeds is below 0.5% (5 differences per 1,000 callable sites), which is within the intraspecific range for C. livia; and (b) in a neighbour-joining tree rooted by the most divergent sample, no breed forms a clade whose mean divergence from all other breeds exceeds 2x the median breed-to-breed divergence. Both conditions must hold.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Any sampled breed, or any monophyletic group of breeds, shows autosomal divergence of 1.0% or more from the other breeds (a level typical of separate Columba species). Alternatively, the tree places a breed group as a deep, well-supported lineage (bootstrap at least 90%) separate from the rest, consistent with descent from a separate wild stock. Either result refutes the claim. Results between 0.5% and 1.0% are inconclusive and must be reported as such.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'Columba livia with its geographical sub-species' is read as the single biological species C. livia, including its wild and feral populations. 'Aboriginal wild stocks' is read as separate wild species or deeply diverged lineages that could have been domesticated independently. 'All our domestic breeds have descended' is operationalised as monophyly and low divergence of breed genomes within one species-level gene pool. This is a modern reinterpretation: descent is inferred from genome-wide SNP divergence and tree topology, not from morphology or breeding experiments. Limits: the dataset's main purpose is the C. livia reference genome assembly (a single bird), and the linked resequencing runs come from Shapiro et al. 2013 (Science). Before analysis, the exact list of breeds and runs must be read from the BioProject's SRA and BioSample records. The test covers only the breeds actually sampled, which is a weaker scope than 'all breeds'. Any outgroup comparison (e.g. another Columba species) would need data outside this one dataset, so the 0.5% and 1.0% thresholds are set from published intra- versus inter-species divergence in Columba.

dataset.name: Columba livia (rock pigeon)
dataset.publisher: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), BioProject
dataset.why_it_fits: The BioProject, titled 'Columba livia (rock pigeon)', is described as whole-genome de novo sequencing of C. livia. It links to the scaffold-level assembly GCA_000337935.2, about 61 BioSamples and 62 SRA experiments, and to the 2013 Shapiro et al. Science paper on pigeon genomic diversity. Raw reads can be downloaded from SRA and the assembly from the NCBI Assembly database. Fields used: SRA run accessions, BioSample attributes (breed or population), and read data for SNP calling against the assembly. From these, pairwise divergence and tree topology can be computed to decide the test.
